rationale: The available literature does not support the hypothesis. While individual case reports (such as Tonduti et al., 2015) demonstrate that adolescent/adult NFU1-related spastic paraplegia (SPG93) can manifest with mixed sensorimotor polyneuropathy in the second or third decade, there is no cohort of 16 or more patients over age 10 with systematic electrophysiological evaluations in the literature, making the quantitative claim of '≥8/16 (≥50%)' completely unsubstantiated. Furthermore, NFU1 mutations predominantly present in infancy as severe, early-onset lethal mitochondrial encephalopathy (MMDS1) rather than isolated spastic diplegia, and evidence is lacking to establish that peripheral neuropathy is consistently absent under age 5.

evidence.text: Tonduti et al. (2015) described a single patient with a milder NFU1 mutation presenting with slowly progressive spastic paraparesis, white matter lesions, and a subacute mixed sensorimotor demyelinating neuropathy emerging in the third decade (electrophysiology evaluated at 18 years of age). This represents a single case report rather than a large cohort.

conflicts: The hypothesis posits a specific cohort sample size and penetrance (≥8/16 individuals over 10 years of age), but SPG93 literature to date consists primarily of single isolated case reports and small familial descriptions rather than structured cross-sectional electrophysiological cohorts.

Most NFU1 mutations lead to lethal infantile encephalopathy with pulmonary hypertension (MMDS1) in infants under 2 years of age; the spastic paraplegia phenotype (SPG93) is an exceptional allelic variant rather than a common toddler cerebral palsy presentation with verified absent neuropathy across cohorts.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true prevalence and timing of subclinical peripheral neuropathy on nerve conduction studies in surviving NFU1/SPG93 patients across international neurometabolic registries?
new_directions.rationale: Systematic collection of neurophysiological data from rare disease registries is needed to establish whether peripheral neuropathy is an obligatory age-dependent feature of SPG93.

new_directions.question_text: Which specific hypomorphic NFU1 missense alleles preserve residual iron-sulfur cluster assembly sufficiently to permit long-term survival with spastic paraplegia rather than infantile lethal MMDS1?
